- When using this in an unsaved file the changes get mixed up with the code from disk.
- Doesn't seem to work for constants and signals at all at the moment
- Doesn't pick up usages as type hint:
```gdscript
class Test:
	pass

var with_type: Test
```
- The following scenario with two scripts:
```gdscript
# a.gd
extends Node
class_name Test1

const SIZE_EXPAND = 1

static var USUAL = 2
```
```gdscript
# b.gd
extends Node

func ready(delta: float) -> void:
	Test1.SIZE_EXPAND # Renaming SIZE_EXPAND will modify b.gd but not a.gd
	Test1.USUAL # Renaming USUAL will modify a.gd but not b.gd
	pass
```
Without having looked at the implementation: Collecting all usages and replacing them needs to happen in two passes, or the change might destroy references that can not be found anymore.
- Shadowing:
```gdscript
extends Node

var delta: float # Renaming delta will rename the parameter name as well but not the usages
func test(delta: float): # Renaming delta will change the occurence in print but not the standalone occurence
	print(delta) # Renaming delta will change the parameter name but not the standalone occurence
	delta # Renaming delta will change the parameter name and the occurence in print but not the standalone occurence

```
Could a 'Match Case' functionality be considered for this? Something like renaming `test` to `test_renamed` also changes `TEST` to `TEST_RENAMED`, `Test` to `TestRenamed`, etc.?

I did a test in a rather complex project. Renaming classes seems to work overall, but it does not rename type hints (as already reported above).

HOWEVER if you have 2 nested classes of the same name, e.g.
```GDScript
class Class1
	class Nested
		pass

class Class2
	class Nested
		pass
```
Renaming `Class1.Nested` will also rename `Class2.Nested`. It will however correctly rename references.

There is something wrong with renaming things in the current file. It works with classes, but seems to fail with enum names, members and constants (and probably more, but that's what I tested). If you try to rename them, they will get renamed correctly everywhere except the file where you started the rename.

Phew! I finally found out why the tests failed. It was because when I created `make_refactor_rename_context()`, I pretty much duplicated all the `make_completion_context()` calls, and renamed them to the new function name. The issue was that inside these calls were variables increments in some of those (i.e. `chain_index++` as the last argument). This caused naturally some errors.

It was fixed by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102380/commits/3d609b09a680d5f0d50af51df98c7011d2c0a1dc
